children: Corient is continuing its international expansion with the acquisition of FortCay Family Advisory, a wealth manager based in the Cayman Islands that oversees $2.6 billion of client assets. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

FortCay is led by advisors Billy Harty and Matt Houghton, who founded the firm in 2023 along with Hank Swartout and Blake Ducharme. The practice provides family office services to a small roster of clients-Corient says FortCay serves just 14 families.

Harty says the two firms share a high-touch service model in their work with wealthy clients and joining Corient will provide his team with additional resources to enhance those relationships. He cites Corient's operating model, which encourages multiple advisors with different areas of expertise to work with individual clients.
"Their partnership model gives us access to the depth and scale of a global firm while creating new opportunities for our clients," Harty says. "We're excited about what lies ahead."

Corient, a Miami-based wealth manager that began life as part of Canada's CI Financial, has been expanding its international operations over the past year through several acquisitions, beginning with the purchase of Stonehage Fleming and Stanhope Capital Group, U.K.-based wealth managers that oversaw more than $214 billion in client assets at the time Corient announced the deal. The firm has since announced the acquisition of a Swiss wealth manager with $10.7 billion in assets and entered into an agreement with its Canadian parent to acquire a portion of CI's ultrahigh-net-worth advisory business. Corient says it manages around $572 billion in client assets.
Corient CEO Kurt MacAlpine notes that the latest acquisition plants a flag in a lucrative market favored by ultrawealthy investors around the world.

"A meaningful share of the world's most complex family wealth is structured and administered in the Cayman Islands," he says. "Many of our clients live, work, and invest across borders-establishing a presence in Cayman deepens our ability to serve them."
A company spokeswoman indicates that more international deals are to come.

"Corient's broader strategy is to continue building a global ultrahigh-net-worth wealth management business," the spokeswoman says. "The firm has expanded across [Europe, the Middle East, and Africa] and India while continuing to pursue opportunities in the U.S., and the Cayman Islands represents another step in that global expansion."
